title: Switches - CS / IOS XE software versions IOS XE 26.2.1 changelog

announcements.post_subject: A new Beta CS Switch firmware is now available

preamble: Important notes

Starting with IOS XE 26.2.1, cloud configuration source switches will follow standard IOS XE CDP behavior and use the hostname as the device identifier. In previous releases the system MAC address is used as the device ID.
Release summary

IOS XE 26.2.1 expands cloud-managed IOS XE support across additional Cisco smart and industrial switching platforms, including the C9350, C9550, and IE9300. The release also introduces Cisco Live Protect support for C9350 and C9550 switches operating in Cloud Config mode.
Release highlights
Expanded platform support for C9350, C9550, and IE9300 switches.

The Security Advisories Dashboard feature identifies Cisco security advisories relevant to your organization and maps them to affected devices. When a Live Protect Shield is available, eligible devices running IOS XE 26.2.1 release can deploy the Shield as an interim mitigation until the corresponding software fix is applied.
Before you upgrade or migrate: key considerations

Please refer to the documentation to review key considerations: https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE/Product_Information/Overviews_and_Datasheets/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE_Overview#Before_You_Upgrade_or_Migrate:_Key_Considerations

Please refer to the documentation to familiarize yourself with management interface architecture changes across MS/CS/IOS XE firmware: https://documentation.meraki.com/MS/Cloud-Native_IOS_XE/Cloud-Native_IOS_XE_Overview#Changes_in_Behavior

For guidance with migrating L3 switches from CS to IOS XE firmware please refer to the detailed guidance here: https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/Cloud_Management_with_IOS_XE/Install_and_Get_Started/Migrating_Switches_From_CS_Firmware_to_IOS_XE_Firmware

After migrating CLI/DNA managed switches to cloud configuration source, please note that console and SSH access are no longer available. All management access is only available via the Dashboard or the local status page through the rear management port/front panel port.
Downgrades from Cloud Management with IOS XE to any prior CS firmware via the Dashboard is restricted.

To ensure a successful upgrade and continued connectivity post-upgrade, resolve before the upgrade all alerts on the Organization > Alerts page that are associated with the switches being upgraded. Resolve “Bad IP assignment” and “VLAN mismatch” alerts on the uplink interfaces, and stacking related alerts such as “Misconfigured Switch”, “Unconfigured Switch” and “Switch Not Connected to Stack” to ensure a successful upgrade.

Layer 3 switches cannot run DHCP servers on uplink interfaces with IOS XE 17.15+. Post-upgrade, interfaces with both Preferred Uplink and DHCP server configurations will have the DHCP server configuration disabled on that interface.

Switches using the Alternative Management Interface (AMI) will require an L3 SVI to be configured for the same VLAN assigned to AMI. For AMI to work, your network must have AMI configured and your switch must have an SVI configured matching that AMI VLAN.
After upgrading from CS to Cloud Management with IOS XE firmware, port mirroring configurations on module ports will not be retained. Reconfigure port mirroring on module ports following the upgrade.

Cloud-born Catalyst switches (-M) require Meraki licenses, with a 30-day grace period for onboarding to the Meraki Dashboard. Eligible migrated switches can use existing DNA licenses for cloud management until February 1, 2029 - no additional license migration or transfer required. Learn more: http://cs.co/9004hmri2

UDLD now uses Cisco UDLD Aggressive mode on fiber ports and will not be enabled on copper interfaces. Please see https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/MS_-_Switches/Operate_and_Maintain/How-Tos/Unidirectional_Link_Detection_(UDLD) for more details

These advanced layer 3 features are currently not supported on IE3500 and IE9300 switches: BGP, VRF, Rapid Per-VLAN STP (RPVST+), Routed Ports, Loopback, VRRP, User-defined ACLs on VLAN, SmartPort, Encrypted Traffic Analytics (ETA), Detailed Traffic Analytics (on trunk ports, port channels, and uplink modules). In addition, IE3500 expansion modules aren't supported at this time. Stacking is not currently supported for IE9300 switches. Combo ports on IE9300 are monitor-only.

Storm Control behavior differs between different generations of switches. Please see https://documentation.meraki.com/Switching/MS_-_Switches/Operate_and_Maintain/How-Tos/Storm_Control_for_MS for more details.

For C9350 customers, upgrading from version 17.18.1 to any version other than 17.18.2 will result in the upgrade taking longer than normal. This is a result of the included ROMMON upgrade, which will require multiple reboots to complete.

Stacking Limit for C9200L: C9200L series models support stacking configurations of up to 5 members. Please ensure your stacks for these models adhere to this limit. Exceeding 5 members may lead to unexpected behavior. This will be resolved in a future release.
Known issues in 26.2.1
On platforms supporting 50G interfaces, ports that auto-negotiate to 50G may not display the negotiated port speed, resulting in incomplete port information.
During a fast move to cloud management, customers may be unable to apply configuration changes even after their connection is restored.
On S1 switches, stack member uptime may not be reported correctly in Dashboard
Fixed issues in 26.2.1
Fixed an issue that could cause standby switches using SNMPv3 SHA-384 or SHA-512 to repeatedly reload after a switchover.
Fixed an issue that could cause a C9350 switch to lose its dashboard connection when an MTU setting was applied.
Fixed an issue that prevented 200G and 400G interfaces from being configured in Device Configuration mode.
Fixed an issue that could cause an error when resetting ports on some IE switches.
Fixed an issue that could prevent SNMP settings from being configured.
Fixed an issue that could interrupt configuration updates.
Fixed an issue that could cause packet captures to fail on modular switches.
Fixed an issue that could cause configuration updates to fail across switch platforms.
Supported models
Support introduced in 26.2.1:
C9350 and C9550 switches are supported in Cloud Configuration Mode and Device Configuration Mode.
IE9300 switches are supported in Cloud Configuration Mode only.
